scope: PostgreSQL Store and schema plus a narrow States matching-budget source follow-up

tests.pgDriver: actual pinned driver password-request path without networking

findings.issue: Concurrent notification fetches could reorder events and deliver old generation data after reconnect.
findings.remaining: Real PostgreSQL LISTEN ordering, connection loss and resynchronization still require actual integration tests.

findings.issue: Different mutation advisory locks and omitted nested locks did not serialize all changes; nested non-SQL failure could be caught and partially committed.
findings.remaining: Real concurrent sessions, deadlock and failover tests remain open.

findings.issue: password:undefined allowed pg environment and pgpass credential fallback despite intended certificate-only profile.
findings.remaining: Server-side certificate authentication and wrong-certificate refusal need actual PostgreSQL TLS tests.

findings.issue: Transaction timer closed client but left an unresolved application callback and outer transaction promise hanging.
findings.remaining: Connection loss around COMMIT can have an indeterminate commit result; recovery/idempotency must be tested on a real server.

findings.issue: Batch row count alone admitted excessive materialized data, including repeated IDs expanded by downstream parsing.
findings.remaining: Actual PostgreSQL CASE/window aggregate memory and query plans remain unexecuted.

findings.issue: Schema version and role flags alone did not prove deployed access controls.
findings.sourceReview: Admission now rejects role memberships, unexpected ownership, missing enabled/forced RLS and inappropriate schema/version-write grants.
findings.remaining: Exact policy definitions, all grants/default privileges, ownership changes and cross-domain denial must be validated against the real server; per-adapter identity and namespace authorization remain an explicit unresolved product gate.

findings.issue: Each Store formerly opened up to four pool connections plus LISTEN and ran its own expiry sweep.
findings.sourceReview: Pool maximum is now one; listener session advisory lock elects an expiry worker per domain.
findings.remaining: Total adapter connection budget, election failover, transaction contention, expiry backlog and Pi resource/latency tests remain open.

findings.issue: Obsolete listener callbacks and close/initialization/election races could affect new lifecycle state.
findings.sourceReview: Listener identity guards, closed checks, post-election admission and failed-connect reset are present.
findings.remaining: Actual failed-handshake, cancellation and reconnect stress tests remain required.

sourceOnlyObservations: RLS predicates bind current_user to the objects/states domain, with ENABLE and FORCE in schema source; no cross-domain bypass was identified by this source review.
Fixed TLS options require TLS1.3, certificate material, hostname validation and rejectUnauthorized; no downgrade entry point was identified by source inspection.
States per-event glob matching now shares a bounded UTF-8 byte work budget; States contract suite was not independently rerun by this reviewer.
limitations: No native PostgreSQL server started: current environment is UID0-only and PostgreSQL correctly refuses root; no bypass attempted.
No hardware, deployment, full penetration test, IEC certification or CRA conformity approval is provided.
No data migration or production approval follows from these targeted tests.
rerunReason: Store glob matching changed to UTF-8 byte semantics; reran the same ten focused tests against the frozen source.
